## 2. User data model

There is no separate types/models file. The `User` shape is defined inline in two places, and they agree on shape:
- `/workspace/app/UserStats.tsx` (lines 1-5): `{ id: number, name: string, isActive: boolean }`
- `/workspace/app/page.tsx` (lines 7-11): the `useState` array literal uses the same shape, e.g. `{ id: 1, name: 'John', isActive: true }`.

The "status" field is named `isActive: boolean` (not `active` or `status`).

## 3. Existing derived-value computation pattern

There are no `useMemo`, `useCallback`, selector functions, or utility/helper files anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via grep across `app/` and root `.ts*` files — the only hits are the TODO/comment text itself). The one existing example of a derived value is in `/workspace/app/page.tsx`:

```tsx
// Good example: derived value calculated directly
const totalUsers = users.length
```

This is called out explicitly as "the existing pattern" via the comment. The convention demonstrated is:
- Derived values are computed as **plain inline `const` expressions** directly in the component body (no memoization, no separate hook/selector/utility function).
- Named descriptively in camelCase (`totalUsers`).
- Computed once per render directly from the prop/state array using plain JS array methods (`.length` here; presumably `.filter(...).length` for active/inactive counts would follow the same style).
- Rendered directly inline in JSX via `{}` interpolation, e.g. `<p>Total Users: {totalUsers}</p>`.

Given the TODO comment in `UserStats.tsx` explicitly says "Follow the existing patterns in this codebase for derived values," and the only example present is `page.tsx`'s `totalUsers`, the intended implementation is: plain inline consts like `const activeCount = users.filter(u => u.isActive).length`, `const inactiveCount = users.length - activeCount`, `const activePercentage = ...`, computed directly in `UserStats`'s function body without `useMemo`.

## 4. Existing "Stats"/summary components for styling/JSX conventions

There are no other Stats/dashboard/summary card components in the repo. The only styling/JSX reference point is `page.tsx`'s plain, unstyled JSX (no CSS classes, no CSS modules, no Tailwind classes used) — it just uses semantic-ish plain `<div>`, `<h1>`, `<p>` tags with text content and inline ternaries (e.g. `{user.isActive ? 'Active' : 'Inactive'}`). `UserStats.tsx`'s stub already follows this same plain-JSX convention (`<div><h2>User Statistics</h2><p>...</p></div>`), so any completed implementation should likely continue using plain unstyled `<div>`/`<h2>`/`<p>` elements consistent with `page.tsx`.</result>
